plain_description.what: How consistently four label-free MMLU-Pro tree re-draws group the same question triples. They are compared with hierarchical k-means baselines that use the same data, the same leaf count and the same shape (bisecting k-means, and flat k-means followed by merging), with 5 seeds.
plain_description.why: It checks whether the trees' stability is a special property of the tree, or just what any comparable clustering would give.
plain_description.information: Result (no new calls): the trees are as stable as bisecting k-means, not more. Their apparent edge comes from leaving about 12% of triples unresolved. They are more stable than merge-based hierarchies, but bisecting k-means matches them, so this is not a tree property. The registered falsifier fired, and an earlier larger stability gap is no longer read as a tree property.
